title: Design Chat App (WhatsApp)
subtitle: Real-time, persistent messaging with read receipts and presence

stages.title: Stage 1 — HTTP Polling & Relational DB
stages.bottleneck: HTTP polling wastes server CPU resources. Millions of users polling every 2s for new messages will crash the servers. Long database query times for message fetching.
stages.narrative:
**The basic HTTP-based messaging.** Messages are sent via POST requests and stored in PostgreSQL. Receivers poll the server every few seconds to check for new messages.

**Bottleneck:** Extremely wasteful. 99% of poll requests return empty results. PostgreSQL locks rows under high concurrent writes.

stages.title: Stage 2 — WebSockets & Session Store
stages.bottleneck: How to push messages instantly? Need persistent connections. Also need to track which server holds the active connection for each user.
stages.narrative:
**Instant message pushing.** We establish persistent WebSocket connections. When User A sends a message to User B:
1. Server WS 1 checks the Session Store (Redis) to locate User B's active server (WS 2).
2. WS 1 routes the message directly to WS 2.
3. WS 2 pushes the message to User B instantly.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Message Queue & Delivery Receipts
stages.bottleneck: If User B is offline, routing fails. We need a way to buffer messages and manage status indicators (Sent / Delivered / Read).
stages.narrative:
**Handling Offline Users.** If User B is offline (checked via Session store), the message is held in the NoSQL database as 'pending'.

**Delivery Receipts:** On successfully enqueuing the message, User A is notified with a 'Sent' receipt (single checkmark). When User B goes online, they pull pending messages from the queue, returning a 'Delivered' receipt (double checkmark) back to User A.

stages.title: Stage 4 — Scale Presence & Sharded Archives
stages.bottleneck: At 1B+ active chats, Cassandra needs sharding by chat_id. Millions of users changing presence status (online/offline) triggers high traffic. Dedicated presence servers needed.
stages.narrative:
**Production scaling patterns.** Messages are archived in **sharded Cassandra databases** sharded by `chat_id` for quick chronological retrieval.

**Presence system:** We offload user heartbeats to a dedicated Presence Service. Users send heartbeats every 30s. If a heartbeat is missed, they are marked offline. When User A opens User B's chat, they query the Presence Service to fetch the status ('Online' or 'Last seen at...').
